goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 stores feed content as raw_html and renders raw post.cooked without sanitization, enabling persistent same-origin XSS and forum session compromise

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in topic_embed.rb:23, posts are created with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. In post.rb:131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns 'raw' directly without any processing. The content comes from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb:33 uses CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content) or from ruby-readability parsing (import_remote method). In best.html.erb:17, the post.cooked is rendered with 'raw' helper which outputs unescaped HTML. While ruby-readability does filter to specific tags, the RSS feed path in poll_feed.rb passes content through CGI.unescapeHTML and then directly to import(), which stores it as raw_html. This content is then rendered without sanitization in the embed view. This is a real XSS vulnerability - malicious RSS feed content could contain script tags that would execute in the context of the Discourse domain when the embed is viewed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 calls open(url) before URL validation, allowing pipe-prefixed URLs to execute shell commands through Kernel#open

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the code calls `open(url).read` where url comes from the method parameter. In Ruby, Kernel#open with a URL starting with '|' can execute shell commands. However, examining the code flow: line 45 shows `def self.import_remote(user, url, opts=nil)` and line 48 calls `open(url).read`. The URL validation happens in the `import` method (line 11: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`), but `import_remote` is a separate method that can be called directly. Looking at where import_remote is called: in lib/topic_retriever.rb:53 it's called with `@embed_url` which comes from user input. The TopicRetriever does check `invalid_host?` which validates the host matches embeddable_host, but doesn't validate the URL scheme. A malicious URL like '|command' would fail the URI parsing in invalid_host? and return true (invalid), preventing execution. However, the check in import_remote itself at line 48 directly passes the url to open() without scheme validation. If import_remote is called from other paths (like lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 which calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`), the URL could potentially be attacker-controlled. This is a real security concern - Kernel#open with pipe-prefixed strings executes commands.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:14 validates only the initial hostname while open-uri follows redirects, allowing redirect-based SSRF to internal or link-local services

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in lib/topic_retriever.rb the invalid_host? method checks if SiteSetting.embeddable_host matches URI(@embed_url).host. Then in fetch_http, it calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url). In app/models/topic_embed.rb, import_remote uses open(url).read via ruby-readability. The open-uri library in Ruby follows HTTP redirects by default. So an attacker could provide a URL like http://eviltrout.com/redirect that passes the hostname check, but the server at eviltrout.com could redirect to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (AWS metadata) or other internal services. This is a valid SSRF vulnerability - the hostname validation only checks the initial URL, not where redirects lead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:61 absolutize_urls does not rewrite relative links lacking a leading slash, causing them to resolve against the Discourse embed URL

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-70, the code only handles URLs that start with '/': `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')`. Relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g., 'images/photo.jpg' or 'page.html') would not be processed and would remain relative. When the content is embedded in Discourse, these relative URLs would resolve against the Discourse domain rather than the original source domain, causing broken links/images. This is a real correctness bug - the method claims to 'Convert any relative URLs to absolute' but only handles absolute-path references (starting with /), not true relative references.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs as root-relative paths on the article host

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-70, the absolutize_urls method handles URLs that start with '/'. The code checks `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs start with '//' (e.g., '//example.com/image.jpg'), which would match `start_with?('/')` and incorrectly be rewritten. For example, '//cdn.example.com/image.jpg' would become 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg' which is incorrect. This is a real bug - protocol-relative URLs should be handled differently (typically by just prepending the scheme) rather than being treated as root-relative paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114 removes the documented --category option, breaking existing imports and forcing imported topics into the default category

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for lib/tasks/disqus.thor, line 117 shows the removal of `method_option :category, aliases: '-c', desc: "The category to post in"` and lines 144-148 show the removal of the code that used this option (`category_id = nil; if options[:category]; category_id = Category.where(name: options[:category]).first.try(:id); end`). The import method is also changed to use `TopicEmbed.import_remote` instead of `PostCreator.new` with the category parameter. This is a real breaking change - existing users who relied on the --category option to import Disqus comments into a specific category will find their scripts broken, and all imported topics will now go to the default category instead of their specified category.
